body.statement: Suppose explicitly that \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\), and suppose \(Y_u(a,e')\) is constant in \(e'\). For the Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix reduction, let \(\mathcal{G}=\{\Omega\}\) be one complete-randomization cell with a fixed treatment count, require \(\pi\) to be exchangeable under every unit permutation on that cell, and set \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)=\pi(\cdot)\). Condition on a unit permutation sampled independently of \(X\), use it as the fixed deterministic tie order \(\prec\), choose any nondecreasing \(\phi\), and set \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\), where \(T_{\mathrm C}(x,y)=\sum_{u\in U}Z_u(x)\phi(R_u(y))\). Then the bounded-null test reduces to their quantile-null randomization test, Theorem 4 gives the individual \(1-\alpha\) confidence set for each fixed \(\tau_{(k)}(e)\), and Section 5.5 gives the joint simultaneous construction over all effect quantiles. For the Su--Li reduction, let \(\mathcal{U}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_S\}\) be fixed, require \(\pi\) to be a product of mutually independent within-stratum complete-randomization laws with fixed treated counts and exchangeability within every \(U_s\), let \(\mathcal{G}\) be the corresponding partition into fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells, and set \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\). Condition on independently predeclared within-stratum unit permutations as the deterministic tie orders \(\prec_s\), choose every \(\phi_s\) nondecreasing, and set \(T=T_{\mathrm S}\), where \(T_{\mathrm S}(x,y)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{u\in U_s}Z_u(x)\phi_s(R_{su}(y))\). Then the bounded-null optimization is exactly their multiple-choice-knapsack problem and its simultaneous confidence-set inversion.
body.justification: The reduction checks that the new target respects the established no-interference boundary.
body.gap: The comparator results cover precisely these special cases rather than assignment-coupled network fibers.
body.consumer: Implementations can reuse verified no-interference routines whenever the legal relation collapses to partitions.
body.proof_tex:
No interference makes \(Y_u(1,e)-Y_u(0,e)\) the ordinary individual treatment
effect, and the elementary order-statistic equivalence
\[
\sum_{u\in U}\mathbf 1\{\tau_u(e)>c\}\leq r
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\tau_{(N-r)}(e)\leq c
\]
holds for \(r<N\), with the \(r=N\) null vacuous.  In both comparator designs, the
specified \(K\) is a partition kernel and is universally valid by
\(\texttt{thm:universal-validity-iff}\).  The pointwise schedule-supremum argument
in \(\texttt{thm:composite-null-validity}\) therefore makes the frozen worst-case
test an exact randomization test for its own assignment-specific score.  What fails
is the asserted equality with the cited adjusted-outcome tests.

Indeed, use one complete-randomization cell with two units and exactly one treated
unit.  Write \(x_i\) for the assignment treating unit \(i\), set
\(\pi(x_i)=1/2\), let \(K(x_i,x_j)=1/2\), and use \(\phi(r)=r\).  Consider the
no-interference schedule
\[
\theta_1(0,e)=1,\quad \theta_1(1,e)=3,
\qquad
\theta_2(0,e)=0,\quad \theta_2(1,e)=2,
\]
and suppose \(X=x_1\).  The observed vector is \((3,0)\).  The frozen score uses
the assignment-specific outcome vectors \((3,0)\) and \((1,2)\); in each, the
treated unit has ascending rank two.  Hence
\[
p_K(x_1;s_\theta)=\frac12\mathbf 1\{2\geq2\}
+\frac12\mathbf 1\{2\geq2\}=1.
\]
Both individual effects are exactly \(2\), so for \(r=0,c=2\) this schedule is
null-compatible and \(p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{0,2}(x_1)=1\).

The Caughey adjusted-outcome construction at boundary \(2\) instead fixes
\((3,0)-2(1,0)=(1,0)\) while permuting treatment.  The treated rank is then two at
\(x_1\) and one at \(x_2\), giving upper-tail value \(1/2\).  The cited individual
and simultaneous conclusions in
\(\texttt{lem:caughey-quantile-specialization}\) concern this latter construction.
Thus the two tests are not identical.  The Su--Li class contains the same example
as its one-stratum case, so the claimed exact multiple-choice-knapsack reduction is
also not a specialization of the frozen score map, notwithstanding the published
result in \(\texttt{lem:suli-knapsack-specialization}\).  This explicit witness
proves the corrected negative statement.
